item.title: Gradle vs Maven vs sbt in 2026: The Definitive JVM Build Tool Guide
item.description: Your build spends 6 of its 11 minutes compiling code that did not change. The CI agent’s cache keeps getting invalidated by a timestamp plugin. The new hire spent their first morning learning that “the build” is actually three nested Maven modules with a Gradle wrapper bolted on top. Every JVM team has a build-tool horror story, and in 2026 the choice still comes down to three real options: Gradle (the adaptable automation powerhouse, 18,806 stars), Maven (the 20-year-old boring standard, 5,324 stars), and sbt (the Scala-native interactive build tool, 4,943 stars). This guide compares them with live repository data, real configuration files, and the migration traps that actually bite — so you can pick once and stop thinking about it.

item.title: Kotlin Linting in 2026: detekt vs ktlint vs Spotless — Which Tool Actually Keeps Your Code Clean?
item.description: A Kotlin codebase starts clean, and within six months it is a battlefield: half the team formats with Android Studio’s auto-indent, a reviewer keeps moving braces around in comments, and the when expressions nobody dares to touch have grown to 400 lines. If you have ever merged a pull request and then watched the style war erupt in the comments, you know the fix is not another convention meeting — it is a tool that enforces the rules mechanically. The problem is that Kotlin developers now have three serious options — detekt, ktlint, and Spotless — and they overlap just enough to make the choice confusing.

item.title: Open-Source JVM Build Tools Compared: Gradle vs Maven vs SBT vs Bazel
item.description:
Introduction

The JVM ecosystem has an unusually rich landscape of build tools, each embodying fundamentally different philosophies about how projects should be structured, dependencies resolved, and builds executed. Whether you’re managing a single microservice or a multi-language monorepo with hundreds of modules, your choice of build tool has cascading effects on developer productivity, CI performance, and onboarding complexity.
